topic: EXP-684 full-field rewrite of WIN-010 (BOU 2017 eclipse −10.9 nT; dome re-anchor to 2016-03-09; Kp correction; post-event status)
review_scope: Pre-integration review of the replacement text in monitor/analyst/expansions/EXP-684.json field_patches (not yet applied to data/wins.json id=010 at HEAD 59bcf25) plus its cross_surface_patches.
our_argument_summary: EXP-684 keeps 'Std Model Explains' and rebuilds WIN-010 around four pillars: (1) the Sq mechanism predicts eclipse dips without dome parameters (Chapman 1919/1933; Yamazaki & Maute 2017; Kim & Chang 2018), (EXP-684.json:field_patches.detail_evidence.new para 1); (2) FSF = tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) via V12, H(r) inert (field_patches.detail_evidence.new 'The station scaling (FSF)'); (3) the magnitude is imported from 2017 BOU, which the dome disowned (PROS-003) yet still calibrates from (OPEN-009, monitor.py domains #7/#10) — replacing the withdrawn asymmetric-Kp argument with a dome-internal vise (field_patches.detail_verdict_text.new 'The Kp argument, corrected'); (4) a dated post-event status: dome precondition failed, dome posted nothing, our evaluation is late, B1-G-005 missed (field_patches.detail_verdict_text.new 'Post-event status (dated 2026-09-27)'). All ten c16 holes are addressed in substance.

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: monitor.py domain #7: kappa_obs = 10.9/6.5 compared to KAPPA = 1.67 (hardcoded both sides). Domain #10: ecm_eclipse = -18.22*0.95*1.672, observed 'PENDING', pass None, falsification 'Fails if measured anomaly within ±3 nT of 0'. Domain #12: fetch_kp() logs latest NOAA 1-min Kp; pass None, 'Not scored'. No INTERMAGNET fetch exists anywhere in monitor.py.
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: Hardcoded. Eclipse domain can never self-score.
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: Three Kp precondition wordings on predictions.html: 'valid only if Kp < 2 on August 12, 2026'; 'Kp < 2 entire Aug 9–12 window'; 'Requires Kp<2 within 3 hours of totality' (the −17.8 nT ±2 nT EBR/SPT claim, registered 2026-04-04). Plus 'IF Kp ≥ 3 ... not a falsification'.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: EXP-684's monitor.py quotes verified verbatim against the live file. Only interpretive gap: EXP-684 says the 1.672 in domain #10 is the OPEN-009 correction 'applied twice'; Part 6 prose in data/sections.json says it is '1.672 (close to KAPPA)'. monitor.py has KAPPA = 1.67, and 18.22/10.9 = 1.6716, so the double-correction reading is the better fit, but both surfaces assert intent. See hole 11.

code_analysis_tags.monitoring_evidence: monitor.py domain #7 (kappa_obs = 10.9/6.5 vs KAPPA 1.67) and domain #10 (ecm_eclipse literal, observed 'PENDING') are static; no API produces an eclipse observation. EXP-684 keeps the 2017 title (option b), so 'hardcoded' stays correct.
code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Eclipse Sq-current reduction; Kim & Chang 2018 (207 data sets / 100 INTERMAGNET observatories, 1991–2016) find Y up, X/Z/F down, more distinct with larger eclipse magnitude, strongest at |mag lat| 30–50°. The dome's own Tier 1 heading reads 'Magnetic Signal (Globe-Compatible)'.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: 2017 BOU and 2016 GUA observations are public INTERMAGNET archive data predating the dome's 2026-03-06 registration.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: FSF follows from V12 (tan(lat) ratio) but the magnitude is imported (−10.9, then −18.22 re-audit, W004 −22.24).

holes_found.description: Chapman (1933) is cited as support for the eclipse mechanism, but its abstract concludes the opposite. EXP-684 adds it as the eclipse-specific foundation: finding 'Chapman 1919 and, for eclipses specifically, 1933'; detail_evidence 'Chapman (1933 ...) applied it to eclipses specifically'; tldr_evidence 'a mechanism Chapman worked out for eclipses in 1933'. The Crossref abstract (api.crossref.org/works/10.1029/TE038i003p00175, fetched this run) says Chapman inferred what an E-layer Sq system would do in an eclipse, then 'the opinion is expressed that they show no regular magnetic effect of the type here predicted, and that therefore S is probably not produced in the E-layer; but a final decision must await further observations.' A defender who opens the abstract gets the line 'your founding eclipse paper says the effect was not seen'. The TLDR is what readers see first, so this counts as a TLDR factual error (major under the TLDR rule).
holes_found.recommendation: Keep Chapman (1933) only as the first theoretical statement of the effect, and say plainly that Chapman judged the observations available in 1933 did not show it. Add a modern detection for the confirmation, e.g. Malin et al. (2000), 'Geomagnetic signature of the 1999 August 11 total eclipse', Geophys. J. Int. 140:F13, doi:10.1046/j.1365-246X.2000.00061.x (cited in Kim & Chang's reference list; verify before use). Kim & Chang 2018 is the statistical confirmation. Rewrite tldr_evidence to something like: 'a mechanism first proposed for eclipses by Chapman in 1933 and confirmed statistically across INTERMAGNET by 2018'.

holes_found.description: The amplitude expectation is unsourced and leaves out the dome's own re-audit. detail_evidence: 'so the Sq framework expects a depression of order 10 nT there. That is the size of the −10.9 nT value.' No source is given for 'of order 10 nT'. Kim & Chang's abstract gives no amplitude, and Korte et al. (2001), 'Did the solar eclipse of August 11, 1999, show a geomagnetic effect?' (JGR 106:18563, also in K&C's references), shows detection at this level is contested for some events. The same paragraph ignores that the dome re-audited this event to −18.22 nT (range −16.38 to −23.38 by baseline window; model.html OPEN-009, monitor/baseline/05-model.txt). A defender can say we matched our expectation to whichever number suited us. This is the same untraced-number pattern Erratum 1 found in B1-M-001.
holes_found.recommendation: Either cite a quantitative mid-latitude eclipse amplitude for about 93% obscuration under a high Sun, or delete 'That is the size of the −10.9 nT value' and say instead that the Sq framework predicts a depression of several to a few tens of nT (with a source) and that both the −10.9 nT and the dome's −18.22 nT re-audit sit in that range. Add provenance for any number kept.

holes_found.description: The Kp inversion is overstated and relies on picking one Kp slot. finding: 'GFZ Kp shows the 2017 eclipse ran at Kp 1+'. tldr_verdict: 'planetary Kp says it was quiet'. kernel_of_truth: 'its quiet/storm labels run opposite to the planetary Kp record'. detail_verdict_text: 'quieter on the planetary index than the one it calls the quietest on record (2016 at Kp 2o)'. The snapshot (win010-c16-verification-snapshots-20260927.json:gfz_kp.2017-08-21) shows the Boulder eclipse (16:23–19:14 UTC, DE421) spans the 15–18 slot (1.333 = 1+) and the 18–21 slot (2.0 = 2o). The second slot equals 2016's 2o. By the dome's own Kp<2 test, half the 2017 window is not quiet. The whole ordering rests on differences of 1/3 to 2/3 of a Kp unit, so 'opposite' will not survive a defender pointing at the 18–21 slot.
holes_found.recommendation: Reframe the argument as: none of the three eclipses came near storm level (all eclipse-window slots Kp ≤ 2o; G1 = Kp 5), so the dome's 'storm-contaminated' label has no support in the planetary record. State both 2017 slots wherever 1+ is quoted (the finding and tldr_verdict currently give only 1+). Drop 'opposite'/'quieter than the quietest'. The withdrawn-yet-calibrating vise does not depend on the ordering and stays intact.

holes_found.description: The precondition audit lists two dome Kp readings, but predictions.html carries three, and the third is the dome's sharpest dated number. monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt: 'Aug 12 2026 Eclipse Magnetic Anomaly −17.8 nT ±2 nT PENDING — PROSPECTIVE Registered: 2026-04-04 ... ECM formula: ΔB = −18.22 × coverage × FSF = −18.22 × 0.978 × (1 − 0.022) = −17.8 nT ... Requires Kp<2 within 3 hours of totality. Station: EBR or SPT'. EXP-684's post-event status says the precondition 'failed on both of its stated readings'. The 3-hour reading also fails: Ebro totality is about 18:31 UTC (DE421, this run), so the ±3 h window covers the 15–18 (1+) and 18–21 (2+) slots, and 2+ ≥ 2. Leaving it out lets a defender say we ignored the most lenient wording. The five-value Ebro history also attributes −17.8 to 'the ×1.672 correction', while the dome's registered claim prints its own formula, and that formula is itself inconsistent: −18.22 × 0.978 = −17.82, so the printed (1 − 0.022) factor is not applied, and applying it would give −17.43.
holes_found.recommendation: Say the precondition failed on all three stated readings and quote the 3-hour one. Cite the −17.8 nT ±2 nT (2026-04-04) claim as the registered form of the Ebro number, with the dome's printed formula and the note that its (1 − 0.022) factor is not applied. Also note that at eclipse maximum 8 of the 9 stations fell in the 18–21 UTC slot (Kp 2+); only Lerwick's maximum, at 17:58, falls in the 1+ slot.

holes_found.description: 'The dome now cites 2016-03-09' is true of only one dome page. The claim field reads 'BOU 2017 eclipse −10.9 nT (dome now cites 2016-03-09)', and detail_claim says 'The live dome site now cites the 2016-03-09 Pacific eclipse for WIN-010 instead.' The live ai-context page (monitor/baseline/07-ai-context.txt, byte-identical per poller 2026-09-28) still lists 'WIN-010 BOU 2017 eclipse -10.9 nT at 17:20 UTC. Tracks geometry not time.' So the dome's AI-facing summary still asserts the 2017 claim that PROS-003 disowns, and the '17:20 at eclipse maximum' timing that DE421 puts 27 minutes early (maximum 17:47 UTC this run). That is a stronger, dome-internal contradiction than the one EXP-684 uses, and as written the claim field is inaccurate.
holes_found.recommendation: claim: 'BOU 2017 eclipse −10.9 nT (wins.html now cites 2016-03-09)'. In detail_claim or evidence, add that the dome's ai-context.html still presents WIN-010 as the 2017 BOU 17:20 UTC 'tracks geometry' result, which contradicts both wins.html and PROS-003. That makes three dome surfaces giving three positions on one WIN.

holes_found.description: One of our own numbers is wrong. detail_verdict_text says 'Under the AACGM-v2 convention they are 4°–10° lower (EBR 33.3°, SPT 31.1°, COI 32.0°, ...)'. From the values given in the same sentence and in the snapshot (aacgm_vs_dipole), the offsets are EBR 9.6, SPT 11.3, COI 11.7, CLF 6.8, HAD 6.9, NGK 4.0, ESK 5.6, LER 4.3, i.e. 4°–12°, recomputed this run. A defender checking our arithmetic will find it, so this is exactly the provenance failure the new frozen-review rule targets. The correlations were recomputed and are correct: dipole vs geographic r = 0.9908 and AACGM r = 0.9993 over 8 European stations; dome-coverage ratio vs FSF r = 0.834.
holes_found.recommendation: Change '4°–10°' to 'about 4°–12°'. Optionally note that GUI's AACGM value (8.3°) is unreliable at that latitude, which is why it is left out.

holes_found.description: The post-event paragraph was written before Erratum 1 (commit 9f1a184) and now contradicts or predates it. It says 'The frozen file stays unedited; the correction goes in a dated erratum' and 'Our §4.2.7 figures ... are corrected there'. The erratum now exists (predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-erratum-2026-09-27.json, OTS upgraded to a Bitcoin attestation in 59bcf25), and §4.2.7 and the eclipse page are already corrected. The symmetry sentence invokes B1-M-001's Kp<2 condition, but the paragraph does not disclose Erratum 1's E-2/E-3 findings on the same claim (mis-cited source; band met on 17 of 30 control days). A reader who sees us say 'what separates the two sides is that we will publish ... including misses' and then finds erratum E-3 elsewhere will ask why it was left out here. Separately, 'The escape clause this entry warned about has now fired' plus 'We cannot count the dome's Kp escape clause against it' reads as choosing option (B) of the operator's still-open symmetric-labelling decision (CLAUDE.md, 2026-09-28 update). A WIN panel should not pre-empt the RESULTS file.
holes_found.recommendation: Link the erratum by path, use past tense, and add one sentence: 'Erratum 1 also records that our B1-M-001 source was mis-cited and that its amplitude band is met on ordinary days, so it had little discriminating power as registered.' Replace the two escape-clause sentences with neutral wording: 'Both sides' magnetic claims were conditioned on Kp < 2, and that condition was not met; how both are labelled will be set symmetrically in the reviewed RESULTS file.'

holes_found.description: CROSS-SURFACE (decider-facing): some of EXP-684.cross_surface_patches are stale. (a) The §4.2.7 patch (old '≈ 88 % obscuration (NASA SE2026Aug12T Besselian elements ...') is superseded: data/sections.json now reads '≈ 94 % obscuration (magnitude 0.949) at 18:15 UT ... JPL DE440s' (9f1a184), so the old substring no longer matches. (b) The docs/eclipse-2026/index.html patch is superseded ('Hartland 88%' count = 0; page already says 94% with an #our-errors link), and its replacement text commits to '15 October 2026', which contradicts the operator decision of 2026-10-31 recorded in EXP-684.operator_decisions. Applying it would publish two different public dates. (c) Still needed: the Hartland SVG alt text in sections.json still says 'about 88%', and KS-005 dome_prediction currently says 'monitor.py computes −29.1 nT', when the actual figure is −18.22 × 0.95 × 1.672 = −28.94.
holes_found.recommendation: Decider: skip patches (a) and (b) and do not use the 15 October string anywhere. Apply (c): the SVG alt text, KS-005, and the separate SVG-regeneration ISS. Check for any remaining 'will be corrected' wording against what 9f1a184 already did.

holes_found.description: The 2016 timing is slightly off. EXP-684 gives the Guam eclipse as 00:22–03:00 UTC and the Boulder local window as 17:22–20:00 MST 'around dusk'. DE421 (this run) gives GUA 00:22–03:24 UTC with maximum 01:52 (84.1% obscuration). The Sun at Boulder was 6.5° up at 00:22 UTC and set around 01:10 UTC, so most of the window was after dark, not 'around dusk'. This strengthens the local-time confound rather than weakening it.
holes_found.recommendation: Use 00:22–03:24 UTC and '17:22–20:24 MST, starting just before sunset and mostly after dark'. Keep the 'our inference' flag.

holes_found.description: The 'within 24h' quote is misattributed. Post-event text: 'well past the dome's own "within 72h" and "within 24h" statements'. On predictions.html, 'within 24h' describes INTERMAGNET data availability (Tier 1 instrument line: 'available within 24h post-eclipse'). The dome's own commitment is 'Post-eclipse: Pull INTERMAGNET + IGETS within 72h. Registry: Post raw plots, r-values, asymmetry index, verdict — public record.'
holes_found.recommendation: Quote the 72h pull-and-post commitment as the dome's deadline and describe 24h as the dome's statement that the data would be available.

holes_found.description: Our surfaces disagree about what the 1.672 in monitor.py is. EXP-684 says the ×1.672 correction was 'applied twice and Ebro's FSF (1.029) is dropped'; Part 6 prose in data/sections.json says '1.672 (close to KAPPA ...) as the FSF multiplier'. monitor.py defines KAPPA = 1.67, while 18.22/10.9 = 1.6716, so the double-correction reading fits better. Both surfaces still state intent that the code does not reveal. Also, OPEN-009 says 'Multiply ... by 1.67', not 1.672 (1.672 is from monitor.py and predictions.html).
holes_found.recommendation: State the fact both surfaces agree on: monitor.py puts 1.672 in the FSF slot where Ebro's 1.029 belongs, and 1.672 matches the OPEN-009 re-audit ratio (18.22/10.9), so the correction appears twice. Harmonize the Part 6 sentence the same way and quote OPEN-009's '1.67' as written.

stronger_arguments.description: Three dome surfaces give three positions on WIN-010: wins.html (re-anchored to 2016, 'Globe has no mechanism'), predictions.html Tier 1 ('Magnetic Signal (Globe-Compatible) ... competing mechanism exists'), and ai-context.html (still 2017 BOU '17:20 UTC. Tracks geometry not time.'). PROS-003 says the 2017 minima did not track geometry, and DE421 puts Boulder's maximum at 17:47 UTC. This contradiction is internal to the dome and needs none of our physics.

The dome itself calls its coverage figures 'sky coverage' ('Hartland beats Ebro despite lower sky coverage', E-PRED-B). Quoting that closes the defender's escape that 'coverage' in ΔZ = baseline × coverage × FSF is not obscuration, and it makes the ×2.1 shortfall at NGK/LER (40% vs 85.4%, 42% vs 88.3%, DE421 this run) a straightforward input error.

The Kim & Chang abstract (per search summaries of the ScienceDirect/ResearchGate record) does state the Y up, X/Z/F down pattern and that the effect 'becomes more distinct as the magnitude of solar eclipse increases'. Useful input for ISS-3101: Erratum 1 E-2 listed the component pattern as unverified, but the abstract appears to support it (the 39-eclipse count remains unsupported).

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome is right that eclipses produce measurable ground magnetic dips, and that detection needs quiet conditions. The GFZ record confirms its model.html note that 2017-08-21 was 'geomagnetically disturbed pre-eclipse' (Kp 3o at 06–09 UT; win010-c16-verification-snapshots-20260927.json:gfz_kp.2017-08-21). Its FSF table genuinely follows from its own V12 triangulation (tan-lat ratio reproduced to r = 0.9999; EXP-684.json:field_patches.detail_evidence.new). Its 2016 multi-station timing coherence is real data (monitor/baseline/02-wins.txt WIN-010).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Timing coherence and a latitude ratio are what the Sq mechanism already predicts (Kim & Chang 2018: effect grows with eclipse magnitude and peaks at 30–50° magnetic latitude). The magnitude is imported from an event the dome disowns (PROS-003, 02-wins.txt) while still using it in monitor.py domains #7 and #10 (live monitor.py, fetched this run). The dome's 2026 precondition failed under all three of its wordings (03-predictions.txt; GFZ 2026-08-12 slots 1+/2+), and its code cannot post a result (domain #10 hardcodes observed 'PENDING').

recommended_action_note: Approve EXP-684 for integration after the sentence-level fixes in holes 0–10. The verdict holds and no second full rewrite is needed. Hole 0 (Chapman 1933, including the TLDR) must be fixed before integration; holes 1–7 should be fixed in the same pass; holes 8–10 can follow as minor patches. Decider cross-surface: skip the §4.2.7 and eclipse-page patches (hole 7).

deeper_analysis: Independent recomputation of our side (frozen-review discipline applied voluntarily because this text carries post-event claims). Skyfield 1.55 + JPL DE421, topocentric, 5 s steps: HAD 17:18–18:15–19:09 UT, 94.4%, Sun 12.7° (matches erratum); EBR totality (mag 1.009) max 18:31, Sun 4.7°; SPT 98.8% / 7.2°; COI 97.2% / 10.4°; CLF 92.9% / 7.2°; NGK 85.4% / 3.4°; ESK 91.0% / 13.6°; LER 88.3% / 14.2°, max 17:58; GUI 69.3% / 10.7°. The '3°–14°' Sun-altitude claim and all five ephemeris-vs-dome coverage pairs are confirmed. BOU 2017: 16:23–17:47–19:14 UT, 93.7%, Sun 57.0°, confirming '≈17:46', '93–94%' and '57°'. GUA 2016: 00:22–01:52–03:24 UT (EXP-684's '03:00' is wrong; hole 8). All GFZ Kp values quoted in EXP-684 match the snapshot. monitor.py domain #7/#10/#12 quotes match the live file verbatim. All dome quotes (PROS-003, OPEN-009, Tier 1 heading, 'Globe has no mechanism', BOU std 2.23/8.05/5.59, 'quietest eclipse day on record', 'Registered: Originally 2026-03-06 | Audited: 2026-03-15', three Kp preconditions, 'IF Kp ≥ 3 ... not a falsification') were found in monitor/baseline. Devil's advocate on our own verdict: the strongest dome counter is still 'the Sq mechanism did not predict WHICH stations; FSF did'. Our text answers it correctly: FSF is tan(lat), which tracks magnetic latitude at r ≈ 0.99 across Europe, so it cannot discriminate. The verdict does not depend on any hole above.

advocate_mode: Dome defender's best line against EXP-684: 'You cite Chapman 1933 as the proof, and Chapman says the effect wasn't there; you say 2017 was quieter than 2016, and half the 2017 eclipse was at the same Kp 2o; you say our precondition failed on two readings, and you ignored our 3-hour window.' Holes 0, 2 and 3 close these. None of them touches the verdict.
summary_for_decider: WIN-010 c17 (queue 609): APPROVE EXP-684 with sentence-level fixes. The verdict holds (Std Model Explains). All 10 c16 holes are substantively addressed. New: 1 major (Chapman 1933 abstract says the eclipse effect was NOT observed — the finding/evidence/TLDR use it as support), 7 moderate (unsourced 'order 10 nT'; slot-selective Kp ordering; third dome Kp precondition missing plus the −17.8 ±2 nT claim; ai-context.html still lists 2017 WIN-010; AACGM offsets 4–12° not 4–10°; post-event paragraph predates Erratum 1 and pre-empts the operator's A/B labelling; stale cross-surface patches, including a '15 October' date that contradicts the operator's 2026-10-31), 3 minor. Cross-surface: SKIP the §4.2.7 and eclipse-page patches; APPLY the SVG alt text + KS-005 (−29.1 → −28.9).
